arxiv-1908-00591.title: Set-Based Models for Cryptocurrency Software
arxiv-1908-00591.creator: Gustavo Betarte, Maximiliano Cristiá, Carlos Luna, Adrián Silveira, Dante Zanarini
arxiv-1908-00591.description: Abstract Emin Gün Sirer once said 1 1 1 hackingdistributed.com/2016/06/17/thoughts-on-the-dao-hack . : It’s clear that writing a robust, secure smart contract requires extreme amounts of diligence. It’s more similar to writing code for a nuclear power reactor, than to writing loose web code […] Yet the current Solidity language and underlying EVM seems designed more for the latter.

arxiv-2012-12917.title: Nonparametric approximation of conditional expectation operators
arxiv-2012-12917.creator: Mattes Mollenhauer, Péter Koltai
arxiv-2012-12917.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Mattes Mollenhauer, Péter Koltai. Given the joint distribution of two random variables X X and Y Y on some second countable locally compact Hausdorff space, we investigate the statistical approximation of the L 2 L^{2} -operator P P defined by [ P ​ f ] ​ ( x ) := 𝔼 ⁡ [ f ⁡ ( Y ) ∣ X = x ] {[Pf](x):=\mathbb{E}[f(Y)\mid X=x]} under minimal assumptions.

arxiv-2107-01473.title: Slope and generalization properties of neural networks
arxiv-2107-01473.creator: Anton Johansson, Niklas Engsner, Claes Strannegård, Petter Mostad
arxiv-2107-01473.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Anton Johansson, Niklas Engsner, Claes Strannegård, Petter Mostad. Neural networks are very successful tools in for example advanced classification. From a statistical point of view, fitting a neural network may be seen as a kind of regression, where we seek a function from the input space to a space of classification probabilities that follows the "general" shape of the data, but avoids overfitting by avoiding memorization of individual data points.

arxiv-2107-06087.title: Controlling Solvent Quality by Time: Self-Avoiding Sprints in Nonequilibrium Polymerization
arxiv-2107-06087.creator: Michael Bley, Upayan Baul, Joachim Dzubiella
arxiv-2107-06087.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Michael Bley, Upayan Baul, Joachim Dzubiella. A fundamental paradigm in polymer physics is that macromolecular conformations in equilibrium can be described by universal scaling laws, being key for structure, dynamics, and function of soft (biological) matter and in the materials sciences. Here, we reveal that during diffusion-influenced, nonequilibrium chain-growth polymerization, scaling laws change qualitatively, in particular, the growing polymers exhibit a surprising self-avoiding walk (SAW) behavior in poor and θ \theta -solvents.

arxiv-2112-05475.title: How to Quantify the Security Level of Embedded Systems? A Taxonomy of Security Metrics
arxiv-2112-05475.creator: 1 st Ángel Longueira-Romero, 2 nd Rosa Iglesias, 3 rd David Gonzalez, 4 th Iñaki Garitano
arxiv-2112-05475.description: Abstract Embedded Systems (ES) development has been historically focused on functionality rather than security, and today it still applies in many sectors and applications. However, there is an increasing number of security threats over ES, and a successful attack could have economical, physical or even human consequences, since many of them are used to control critical applications.

arxiv-2208-06292.title: Shape Proportions and Sphericity in n n Dimensions
arxiv-2208-06292.creator: William Franz Lamberti
arxiv-2208-06292.description: Abstract Shape metrics for objects in high dimensions remain sparse. Those that do exist, such as hyper-volume, remain limited to objects that are better understood such as Platonic solids and n n -Cubes. Further, understanding objects of ill-defined shapes in higher dimensions is ambiguous at best.

arxiv-2310-16721.title: Giant Gravitons and non-conformal vacua in twisted holography
arxiv-2310-16721.creator: Kasia Budzik
arxiv-2310-16721.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Kasia Budzik. Twisted holography relates the two-dimensional chiral algebra subsector of 𝒩 = 4 \mathcal{N}=4 SYM to the B-model topological string theory on the deformed conifold S ​ L ​ ( 2 , ℂ ) SL(2,\mathbb{C}) . We review the relevant aspects of the duality and its two generalizations: the correspondence between determinant operators and “Giant Graviton” branes and the extension to non-conformal vacua of the chiral algebra. Introduction and summary 1.1.

arxiv-2410-03719.title: FluentEditor2: Text-based Speech Editing by Modeling Multi-Scale Acoustic and Prosody Consistency
arxiv-2410-03719.creator: Rui Liu, Jiatian Xi, Ziyue Jiang, Haizhou Li
arxiv-2410-03719.description: Abstract Text-based speech editing (TSE) allows users to edit speech by modifying the corresponding text directly without altering the original recording. Current TSE techniques often focus on minimizing discrepancies between generated speech and reference within edited regions during training to achieve fluent TSE performance.

arxiv-2502-10517.title: KernelBench: Can LLMs Write Efficient GPU Kernels? † † footnotetext: *Equal Contribution. Correspondence: aco@stanford.edu, simonguo@stanford.edu
arxiv-2502-10517.creator: Anne Ouyang, Simon Guo, Simran Arora, Alex L. Zhang, William Hu, Christopher Ré, Azalia Mirhoseini
arxiv-2502-10517.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Anne Ouyang, Simon Guo, Simran Arora, Alex L. Zhang, William Hu, Christopher Ré, Azalia Mirhoseini. Efficient GPU kernels are crucial for building performant machine learning architectures, but writing them is a time-consuming challenge that requires significant expertise; therefore, we explore using language models (LMs) to automate kernel generation. We introduce KernelBench , an open-source framework for evaluating LMs’ ability to write fast and correct kernels on a suite of 250 carefully selected PyTorch ML workloads.

arxiv-2507-01169.title: Multi-wavelength observations of substructures in solar flare ribbons
arxiv-2507-01169.creator: Vishal Singh, Eamon Scullion, Gert J. J. Botha, Natasha L. S. Jeffrey, Malcolm Druett, Gerry Doyle, Chris Nelson, Aidan O’Flannagain, Alex G.M. Pietrow
arxiv-2507-01169.description: Abstract Solar flare ribbons are features in the lower atmosphere that show enhanced emission intensity, particularly noticeable in H α \alpha and EUV images of the transition region and upper chromosphere. In this study, we provide observational evidence that the flare ribbons are composed of a large number of coherent sub-structures that we call riblets .

arxiv-2509-08494.title: HumanAgencyBench : Scalable Evaluation of Human Agency Support in AI Assistants
arxiv-2509-08494.creator: Benjamin Sturgeon, Daniel Samuelson, Jacob Haimes, Jacy Reese Anthis
arxiv-2509-08494.description: Abstract As humans delegate more tasks and decisions to artificial intelligence (AI), we risk losing control of our individual and collective futures. Relatively simple algorithmic systems already steer human decision-making, such as social media feed algorithms that lead people to unintentionally and absent-mindedly scroll through engagement-optimized content.

arxiv-2601-19231.title: LLMs Can Unlearn Refusal with Only 1,000 Benign Samples
arxiv-2601-19231.creator: Yangyang Guo, Ziwei Xu, Si Liu, Zhiming Zheng, Mohan Kankanhalli
arxiv-2601-19231.description: Abstract This study reveals a previously unexplored vulnerability in the safety alignment of Large Language Models (LLMs). Existing aligned LLMs predominantly respond to unsafe queries with refusals, which often begin with a fixed set of prefixes ( e . g ., ‘I’m sorry’).

britannica-1911-walton-izaak.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-walton-izaak.description: Article 'Walton, Izaak' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 28), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. original gravestone with its Latin inscription has disappeared; but in 1843 a new monument was erected over the spot. There is also a fine statue of the poet at Bozen, unveiled in 1877. Historically interesting as Walther's political verses are, their merit has been not a little exaggerated by modern German critics, who saw their own imperial aspirations and anti-papal prejudices reflected in this patriotic poet of the middle ages.

pmc-10586943.title: Successful repair of acquired intrathoracic nonmalignant tracheoesophageal fistulas using thoracoacromial artery perforator flap through a midsternal incision approach: a report of three cases
pmc-10586943.creator: Peisong Yuan, Benoit Jacques Bibas, Takuya Nagashima, Hei-Yu Matthew Chen, Camilla Poggi, Fei Chen, Yang Hu
pmc-10586943.description: BackgroundAcquired intrathoracic nonmalignant tracheoesophageal fistulas (TEFs) are rare and challenging surgical problems. They can constitute a life-threatening condition due to severe pulmonary complications and poor nutrition. Surgical treatment is effective for most patients undergoing operative repair. However, in recent studies, the difficult-to-ignore early complications of surgical treatment can be as high as 62.5%.

pmc-10611601.title: Accelerating Machine Learning Inference with GPUs in ProtoDUNE Data Processing
pmc-10611601.creator: Tejin Cai, Kenneth Herner, Tingjun Yang, Michael Wang, Maria Acosta Flechas, Philip Harris, Burt Holzman, Kevin Pedro, Nhan Tran
pmc-10611601.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). We study the performance of a cloud-based GPU-accelerated inference server to speed up event reconstruction in neutrino data batch jobs. Using detector data from the ProtoDUNE experiment and employing the standard DUNE grid job submission tools, we attempt to reprocess the data by running several thousand concurrent grid jobs, a rate we expect to be typical of current and future neutrino physics experiments.

pmc-10643268.title: Refining an ecological momentary assessment study of binge eating among sexual minority and heterosexual young women: a mixed methods pilot study
pmc-10643268.creator: Kristin E. Heron, Charlotte A. Dawson, Cassidy M. Sandoval, Lauren V. Butler, Abby L. Braitman, Alison Cerezo, Robin J. Lewis
pmc-10643268.description: BackgroundEcological momentary assessment (EMA) is used to capture daily lived experiences, states, and environments. Although EMA is commonly used in behavioral health research, there remains a dearth of literature on how researchers account for design considerations of EMA techniques when designing studies.

pmc-11676373.title: Continuous Epidural Versus Non-Epidural Pain Management After Minimally Invasive Esophagectomy: A Real-Life, High-Case-Load Center Experience
pmc-11676373.creator: Sebastian Boehler, Markus Huber, Patrick Y Wuethrich, Christian M Beilstein, Stefano M Arigoni, Marc A Furrer, Yves Borbély, Dominique Engel, Young-Tae Jeon
pmc-11676373.description: Background/Objectives: Esophagectomy is a key component of esophageal cancer treatment, with minimally invasive esophagectomy (MIE) increasingly replacing open esophagectomy (OE). Effective postoperative pain management can be achieved through various analgesic modalities. This study compares the efficacy of thoracic epidural anesthesia (TEA) with non-TEA methods in managing postoperative pain following MIE.

pmc-12509346.title: PD-L1 regulates c-MET phosphorylation and contributes to MET-dependent resistance to osimertinib in EGFR-mutant NSCLC
pmc-12509346.creator: Chia-Chi Hsu, Derek De-Rui Huang, Wei-Hsun Hsu, Min-Shu Hsieh, Fang-Yu Lin, Pei-Chen Tai, Shih-Yun Chou, Hsin-Hui Tsai, Chen-Yuan Tseng, Bin-Chi Liao, Jin-Yuan Shih, James Chih-Hsin Yang
pmc-12509346.description: BackgroundProgrammed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) is a well-recognized predictive biomarker for immunotherapy in non-oncogene-addicted non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, its role in epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mutant NSCLC remains unclear. This study aims to investigate the impact of PD-L1 on the signaling pathways in EGFR-mutant NSCLC.

pmc-12827464.title: Characteristics of crack network catastrophe in highly weathered mudstone under hydro-mechanical disturbance: a cross-scale damage constitutive framework
pmc-12827464.creator: Honghuan Cui, Wei Wan, Biao Ma, Hongyan Guo, Huizhen Wu
pmc-12827464.description: To thoroughly investigate the patterns of crack development and the mechanisms of degradation damage in shallow, highly weathered mudstone subjected to repeated dry-wet cycles, a series of laboratory tests were conducted. Initially, the progression of surface cracks on the specimens was documented through fixed-point photography.

pmc-12830886.title: Silhouettes, number Location, and cube analysis tests from the VOSP battery reveal visual object and space perception deficits in early Alzheimer’s disease
pmc-12830886.creator: Vaiva Sutnikiene, Egle Audronyte, Gyte Pakulaite-Kazliene, Gintaras Kaubrys
pmc-12830886.description: The Visual Object and Space Perception Battery (VOSP) is a widely used tool for evaluating higher visual processing. However, limited information exists regarding its diagnostic utility in differentiating mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and mild dementia (MD) due to Alzheimer’s disease (AD) from cognitively normal older adults (CG).

pmc-13230809.title: DNMT3A drives mitochondrial dysfunction in intracerebral hemorrhage via PGC-1α promoter hypermethylation
pmc-13230809.creator: Jun Zhao, Qiongyan Tang, Lu Lu, Minmin Xu, Chunlin Zhang, Ruifang Ren, Ping Zhang, Jing Cao, Weimin Yang
pmc-13230809.description: Mitochondrial dysfunction drives secondary injury in intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH), yet its upstream regulatory mechanisms remain elusive. This study examines whether ICH-induced DNA methyltransferase 3 A (DNMT3A) activation triggers PGC-1α promoter hypermethylation, causing mitochondrial impairment and neuronal damage through epigenetic silencing of this key metabolic regulator. Both in vitro and in vivo approaches were employed.

pmc-13239060.title: Australian Podiatry Research in Workforce and Education: A Bibliometric Analysis
pmc-13239060.creator: Malia Ho, Peta Tehan, Matthew R. Carroll, Cylie Williams
pmc-13239060.description: BackgroundTo conduct a bibliographic analysis of English language research pertaining to podiatry workforce and education by Australian authors.MethodsThe Scopus database search was conducted to identify all Australian workforce and education‐related articles published by podiatric authors in English from 1970 to 2024. Bibliometric analysis was performed using Biblioshiny, a web‐based graphical interface for the bibliometric R package.
